subject: Mathematics
purpose: Which hosts a research agent may cite, and for what. Tier A is primary authority (curriculum, official papers and answer keys). Tier B may support explanations only. Tier C may be used to LOCATE an item; it becomes secondary authority for a QUESTION or ANSWER_KEY card only through the corroboration fallback below. Any host not listed cannot be cited.

hosts.covers: Curriculum, sample question papers, marking schemes
JEE Main information bulletin and syllabus
JEE Main papers, provisional and final answer keys
JEE Advanced papers, answer keys, syllabus
JEE Main question papers and answer keys as published by NTA on its CDN; the card's QUESTION fields must name the NTA paper exactly
Aggregated JEE Main / Advanced past questions with answers (questions.examside.com)
JEE Main / Advanced paper solutions and answer keys
JEE Main / Advanced paper solutions and answer keys
JEE Main / Advanced paper solutions and answer keys
JEE Main chapter-wise past questions with answer keys
JEE and CBSE past papers with solutions
CBSE board past papers with solutions

corroboration_fallback.when: no Tier A copy of the paper or key can be pinned (the official page is gone, unreachable, or never published the item)

requires.official_attempt: card.corroboration.official_attempt: the Tier A URL tried, its outcome (NOT_PUBLISHED | UNREACHABLE | ITEM_NOT_ON_PAGE) and the date
requires.independence: the card's own source and every corroborating source must be Tier C hosts with different publishers
requires.agreement: each corroborating quote is re-found in its pinned snapshot; for ANSWER_KEY every quote states the same answer, for QUESTION every quote carries the same stem
requires.verifier: the independent verifier solves the question and agrees with the key (the board already requires this for every node)

corroboration_fallback.label: card.authority = SECONDARY_CORROBORATED; the learner product shows it as a secondary source, never as the official paper
corroboration_fallback.never: Tier C never supports DEFINITION, RELATION, CONDITION or any other kind; one Tier C host alone never supports anything but LOCATOR_HINT

local_sources_note: Scanned books and papers the owner holds. Only the owner adds an entry and the SHA-256 of each scan file (print it with scan_ingest.py hash). The scan bytes and OCR text never leave the owner's machine; the repository gets the acquisition record, a scan manifest with a hashed shingle index, and short quotes. Fields: source_id, title, authors, publisher, edition, year, isbn, kind (TEXTBOOK | EXEMPLAR | QUESTION_BANK | EXAM_PAPER | ANSWER_KEY | NOTES), tier (A for official NCERT/CBSE/NTA/JEE material, B for published reference books), may_support (optional narrowing of the tier's kinds), rights (OFFICIAL_PUBLIC | COPYRIGHTED_OWNED_COPY), scan_sha256s, registered_by, registered_at.
